issues.issue: A jury-trial waiver binding "Lender" is difficult to square with c004, which identifies the Lender as a third party that is not a signatory to this Agreement.
The clause speaks of not "reject[ing]" the Arbitration Agreement, while the arbitration section (c093) provides only an "opt out" mechanism, so the trigger is described by an undefined term.

If the arbitration agreement is rejected, this clause leaves the jury waiver operative even though c098 assumes no jury trial only when arbitration is chosen; the interaction with c093–c096 is unresolved.
This compliance savings language duplicates c040 in the LOC section, with slightly different wording covering different actors, raising the usual question of which governs.
The clause restates c041 (the garbled unlawful-excess savings clause in the LOC section) in different terms, so the two savings provisions must be reconciled.
"Amortizing, prorating, allocating and spreading" is left without an object or method, so what may be spread and over what period is unstated.

"Any claim that this agreement or related matter, or any action or inaction by us or Lender, or by any other person, is legally non-compliant, illegal or unenforceable" is drafted so broadly and one-sidedly that its coverage and its status as a condition precedent are open to construction.

A mandatory 60-day pre-suit notice sits awkwardly with c075, which lets either party demand arbitration of a Claim "at any time", and with the arbitration section's silence on any notice-and-cure condition.
Notice to the Lender is directed to PLS's own Chicago legal department, which conflicts with c004's identification of DSI Lending Resources as a separate third-party lender.
"Any corrective action shall relieve us and Lender of any liability" does not say what corrective action suffices or whether it must actually cure the claim.

"Reasonable attorneys' fees ... regardless of whether legal proceedings are actually filed, and all costs and disbursements" leaves both the reasonableness measure and the scope of "all costs and disbursements" open.

"A person may not threaten or pursue criminal charges" does not say who is bound or whether it creates any contractual promise by PLS, and the exception ends in the open catch-all "or other criminal conduct" after forgery, fraud and theft.

The restriction on pursuing criminal charges over a check given as security is in direct tension with c044, which gives PLS the right on default to "seek collection of any check or similar security you have provided us" and any other remedy allowed by law.
"You and we agree to arbitrate Claims instead of having them decided in court" is stated as an unconditional commitment, though the mechanism that follows is elective and revocable.

The flat agreement to arbitrate instead of litigating cannot be squared with c074/c075 (arbitration only "upon the election" of a party, even after a lawsuit is begun), c047 ("we are not required to ... arbitrate") and the opt-out in c093.

"Claim" sweeps in "the actions of you, us, Lender, or third parties" and "any products or services offered to you", a boundless catch-all beside the specific enumerated agreements, and limb (e) purports to delegate the validity of the arbitration agreement itself.

The exclusion in limb (i) for loans "in connection with which you properly exercised an opt-out right" must be read against c096, which excludes only claims "arising under this Agreement", leaving the opt-out's reach unresolved.

Expanding "we" and "us" to affiliates, agents and owners for arbitration purposes conflicts with the c003 definition limiting those words to PLS Loan Store of Texas, Inc., and determines whether non-signatories may compel arbitration.
Arbitration arises only "upon the election" of a party, yet the same sentence says any Claim "shall be resolved by binding arbitration", mixing permissive and mandatory language.
The election mechanism sits against c071's unconditional "we agree to arbitrate Claims instead of having them decided in court", so whether arbitration is automatic or must be invoked is contestable.

"At any time, even if the other party has begun a lawsuit" says nothing about conduct short of a lawsuit and does not address whether the right to demand arbitration can be waived by inconsistent litigation conduct.
Read with c046 (delay in enforcing rights does not lose them) and c076 (no arbitration after judgment), the provision leaves unclear whether invoking other legal processes forfeits arbitration.
"Matters included in the judgment" and "a lawsuit involving you, us, or Lender" leave uncertain which prior proceedings, including criminal or third-party proceedings, cut off the arbitration right.

After naming two specific organizations the clause adds "any other arbitrator ... reasonably satisfactory to us", a general catch-all controlled by one party, and it conflates selecting an arbitration organization with selecting an individual arbitrator.

This clause forfeits the customer's right for failing to select "an arbitrator" within 20 days, whereas c077 gives the customer the right to select an arbitration organization, and c079 assumes the parties must "agree" on an arbitrator.
"If we are not able to agree on another arbitrator" does not say with whom agreement is required, and "the named organization" has no clear antecedent given the list in c077.
Defaulting to the AAA Rules for Consumer Arbitrations may be inoperative because c081 and c107 bar selecting any organization whose rules permit class arbitration or reject the class waiver.

"Permits class actions in arbitration" is untested against organizations whose rules neither authorise nor forbid them, and it duplicates but does not match c107's "does not accept this class action waiver".
The cap is measured by "what your court costs would have been if the Claim had been resolved in a state court with jurisdiction", a hypothetical figure the clause gives no method for calculating.
The FAA choice must be read with c110, which applies Texas law to the Agreement generally but the FAA to the arbitration agreement, and with c087's direction that the arbitrator "apply relevant law".
Three alternative venues are listed without saying who chooses among them, and "such other location as we or Lender may agree" does not identify with whom agreement is needed.

Directing the arbitrator to "apply relevant law" while forbidding federal or state rules of procedure or evidence leaves it unclear how substantive law with embedded procedural content is to be applied.
The contemplation of a possible in-person hearing must be read against c086's venue rule, which assumes a hearing "at which you must appear in person".
Each party bearing its own attorneys' fees is in tension with c063 and c031, which make the customer liable for PLS's attorneys' fees and costs of collection.
The deeming provision fixes the place of the award by the customer's "home address" at the time of the decision, which may be nowhere connected to the arbitration venue set by c086.
The opt-out right for "Claims arising under this Agreement" is narrower than the c072 definition of Claim, which reaches prior agreements, other products and the actions of third parties.
The opt-out notice must be sent to "PLS Financial Services", an entity that is not the defined "we/us" in c003 and not the addressee for notices under c060.
"Arising under this Agreement" is a narrower formula than the "arising from or relating to" language defining Claim, so the effect of an opt-out on the wider class of Claims is uncertain.

The limitation cannot readily be squared with c072, which defines Claim to include disputes about prior agreements, other products and third-party actions, all of which the opt-out apparently leaves arbitrable.

Making prior and subsequent transactions arbitrable under their own agreements is difficult to reconcile with c072(b), which folds any prior credit services agreement or loan into the Claims covered here.
The statement that neither party can litigate a Claim once arbitration is chosen sits against c075, which permits an arbitration demand even after a lawsuit has begun, and c076's judgment carve-out.
The waiver is conditioned on someone choosing arbitration ("If either you, we, or Lender ... choose arbitration"), while c101–c104 state the class waiver unconditionally.
